newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Five Palestinians wounded in West Bank clashes.
newsitem.headline: Five Palestinians wounded in West Bank clashes.

text.p: Israeli troops wounded five Palestinian demonstrators in the West Bank village of Sourif on Monday, Palestinian sources said.

They said the clashes broke out when the Israelis sealed off the village and brought in a bulldozer to demolish the home of a resident who was arrested recently for involvement in a series of attacks on Israelis.

The sources said a 16-year-old Palestinian boy was in serious condition with a gunshot wound in his neck and had been evacuated to a Hebron hospital. Another person was wounded with live ammunition and three were shot with less lethal rubber bullets, they said.
An Israeli army spokesman confirmed that the army used rubber bullets in the clash and said: "We have no information about the use of live ammunition."

Sourif, in a part of the West Bank still under Israeli control after Israel transferred eight towns to Palestinian self-rule, was the home of an Islamic bomber who killed himself and three Israeli women in a Tel Aviv cafe last month.
Earlier this month Israeli and Palestinian security forces uncovered an Islamic Hamas cell of six Sourif residents suspected of killing several Israelis in a series of attacks over two years.

The village was under Israeli curfew for 27 days after the Tel Aviv bombing. Palestinians said residents were frustrated on Monday when the Israeli army sealed the village again after it had been open for only three days.
